THE SAME-VALUE STATEMENT BELOW HOLDS FOR THE POSITION AND NOT FOR THE INDEX: the index is stopped by each arm's own equality check (the default sameValueGuard of OIMSingleComputed, and alien's computed comparison), which is what this row prices. ARCHITECTURAL POINT: a value written every frame whose consumer wakes rarely, which is the shape of a virtualised list under scroll. Ours enlists the effect on the write, and at the flush the effect asks the index, which re-derives, finds the same value and stops. Alien-signals propagates pending flags to the computed and the effect on the write, and the effect checks the computed, which re-derives and stops. Browsers dispatch scroll at most once per rendered frame, so k1 is the scroll case; k4 is a handler that moves the position several times. Ours is @oimdb/core from source: an OIMSingleEntity root written through entityContentService.updateEntityColumn, OIMSingleComputed nodes for anything derived, one effect from OIMEffectService, and channel.flush() as the settle. The floor is alien-signals 3.2: signal, computed, effect, and startBatch/endBatch where the row says so. Every write stores a new number from a counter, so no write on either arm is stopped by a same-value check. Each arm runs in its own process.
